attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, endorsed. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: Present-tense observation. The normalised text drops the scope qualifier 'In the current relationship', though the contract keeps it. The core meaning holds: OpenAI lacks the means to fund its Oracle commitment.

contract.note: The reading compares cash plus secured financing at publication against the multiyear Oracle commitment, taking payment timing into account. That is an ordinary, fair reading of 'have the money' given the $300B context. The result depends on that interpretation.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own disclosure that the Oracle partnership exceeds $300B over five years. It gives the size of the commitment but no payment schedule and nothing on OpenAI's resources.
The NVIDIA investment is a letter of intent and arrives in stages as capacity is deployed, so it is not secured cash. It does not show the size of any funding gap.
The March 2025 SoftBank financing of up to $40B, with conditions. It shows OpenAI had resources beyond cash, but there is no reconciliation as of September 29.

reviews.rationale: The packet does not establish OpenAI's cash and secured financing on September 29, 2025, or the Oracle payment schedule. The items show the scale of the commitment and some staged or conditional financing, but none reconciles resources against obligations. The evidence cannot settle whether existing funds were insufficient.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his newsletter, endorsed.

semantics.note: The normalisation keeps both conjuncts: more than $500B has gone into the industry, and no model or model-product company is profitable. Kind is observation.

contract.note: Reading 'profitable' as company-level earnings in the latest reportable period, and 'investment' as money actually invested, is a fair, ordinary reading of the present-tense claim. The industry boundary and accounting basis are supplied by the evaluator.

evidence.note: TIME reports that Midjourney was profitable within a year of its 2021 founding. That is about an earlier period, gives no earnings figure, and is not the applicable 2025 period, so it does not meet the contradiction condition.

reviews.rationale: No reconciled cumulative investment total was found, and no comprehensive profitability data for the relevant 2025 period. The Midjourney report raises doubt about the universal 'no profitable company' claim, but it concerns 2022 and gives no defined earnings. The packet cannot settle either part of the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words and estimates, endorsed.

semantics.note: The 2025 burn figure is stated firmly ('$8 billion or more') for a year not yet complete, so it is a scored forecast. The 2030 figure carries 'if my estimates are right' and is preserved and excluded from scoring.

contract.note: Net cash burn over calendar 2025 is the ordinary meaning of 'burn'. Excluding the hedged 2030 estimate is fair. Judging at the reported precision is reasonable, but the reported $8B is rounded and sits right at the threshold.

evidence.note: CNBC (February 2026), citing sources, reports that OpenAI burned $8B in 2025, below its $9B target. This is the realized full-year figure on a net burn basis and meets the '$8B or more' threshold at the reported precision.

reviews.rationale: Calendar 2025 is over. Credible reporting from before the evaluation date puts OpenAI's realized 2025 burn at $8B, which meets the 'or more' threshold. One caveat: the figure is unaudited and rounded. The hedged 2030 estimate is not scored.
